newsitem.title: DENMARK: NOVO TO ALTER ACCOUNTING PRINCIPLES.
newsitem.headline: NOVO TO ALTER ACCOUNTING PRINCIPLES.

text.p: Danish pharmaceutical group Novo Nordisk said on Wednesday that it was changing its accounting principles from January 1, 1998, bringing them into line with United States standards.
In a statement accompanying its first half 1997 results it listed the following changes:
Production costs would be included in inventory valuations.
Goodwill from the acquisition of businesses as the difference between purchase price and net assets acquired would be capitalised and amortised over the expected useful lives.
Deferred tax would be provided for all temporary differences between financial and tax reporting.
Interest incurred in connection with the financing of major investments in property, plant and equipment would be capitalised and depreciated as an integral part of total capital expenditure.

"These changes, which will result in a higher degree of comparibility between Novo Nordisk's financial statements and those of other international companies....will in all essentials be in harmony with U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles," it said. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +(45) 33 969650
